A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-F are readable and support a reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix F report original nonlinear-system simulations, including estimator comparisons and sensitivity results in Figures 1 and 2.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix F report original simulations comparing estimators and analyzing parameter sensitivity, with results in Figures 2 and 3.

M1.justification: Equation (12) changes the proposed objective from a sum of vector ℓ1 residual norms to a sum of unsquared ℓ2 residual norms. This changes the optimization procedure and how observation coordinates contribute to estimation; it is not merely a renamed estimator.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic partially observed nonlinear systems, using Gaussian and nonzero-mean uniform inputs and both tanh and signed-logarithmic activation functions. No dataset, application domain, or task coverage is added.

E2.justification: Least squares remains a comparator. V2 adds explicit comparisons of the proposed ℓ2 estimator against ℓ1 and ℓ∞ estimators under both input distributions in Figures 2(b) and 3(b). The ℓ1 estimator was the proposed method in v1.

E3.justification: The memory-length/contraction-factor sweep is restricted to uniform inputs in v2, whereas v1 tests it under both Gaussian and uniform inputs. The added norm comparison reuses the existing settings. Both appendices retain the same dimensions, 80:20 kernel-fitting split, and stated horizon T = 500.

E4.justification: V2 adds a norm-choice analysis comparing α = 1, 2, and infinity, while removing the Gaussian-input memory/contraction sensitivity panels. Uniform-input sensitivity and the bounded-versus-unbounded activation analysis remain, now reporting the ℓ2 estimator.

E5.justification: Both Appendix F sections specify 95% confidence intervals based on standard errors from 10 experiments with randomized system matrices and disturbances. No changed run count, seed disclosure, or statistical reporting procedure is identified.

E6.justification: V2 adds the finding that ℓ2 has the smallest error among the tested norm estimators, with relatively small empirical differences, in Figures 2(b) and 3(b). Other panels report replacement ℓ2 trajectories, and Gaussian sensitivity results are removed. Least-squares vulnerability and the memory/contraction trends remain.

T1.justification: V2 introduces bounded basis-approximation error into the model and Theorem 3.1, revises the basis Lipschitz condition and Bernoulli attack-mask assumption, and substantially replaces Appendix D's coordinatewise sign-symmetry analysis with a matrix-norm argument. Sample-complexity dependence changes. The stated upper and lower error bounds lose v1's explicit square-root-of-observation-dimension factor, and Appendix E removes the corresponding replicated-output construction.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion transfer the central optimal-estimation claim from ℓ1 to ℓ2. The introduction explicitly allows finite-basis approximation error, and v2 argues for observation-dimension-independent error bounds and weaker guarantees for other norms. The broad adversarial input-output identification objective remains.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explanation of norm choice in Remark 3.4, qualifies accuracy by sufficiently small approximation error, and motivates the setting through detectable versus undetectable attacks and nonzero-mean controller inputs. The memory-length tradeoffs and the lower-bound caveat concerning time-dependent attack magnitudes remain.

D1.justification: Appendix F retains the hardware description, MOSEK solver, polynomial-kernel construction, regularization grid, data-generation instructions, initial state, and attack distributions. No new code/data access information or additional implementation disclosure is identified beyond the changed estimator definitions.

R1.justification: V2 adds attack-detection references by Fawzi et al., Shoukry and Tabuada, and Pajic et al., plus Lin et al. and Kim and Lavaei's batch/streaming work. Khalil and Sontag references are removed. Broad positioning and Table 1 remain; publication updates to retained works do not constitute new comparators.

P1.justification: V1's separate Model Justification subsection is substantially condensed and redistributed across the introduction and Appendix A. V2 reorganizes the formulation into four explicit steps, reorders assumptions, and rewrites the analysis outline. These are substantial narrative changes beyond estimator-name substitutions.

P2.justification: V2 adds a two-panel conceptual Figure 1, replaces the middle panels of both experimental figures, and changes legends and displayed time ranges. It also substantially reformats the title block, headings, page headers, and content placement. Table 1 is retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 improves scope clarity by propagating basis-approximation error through Theorem 3.1, addressing v1's exact representation despite numerical approximation, and adds direct evidence for norm choice. The gain is limited: approximation error is not quantified for the fitted kernels, empirical norm differences are modest, Gaussian sensitivity plots are removed, and the lower-bound limitation concerning time-dependent attack magnitudes remains.
